slot.brief: A Zener regulator with a series resistance and varying input voltage; find the current through the Zener when the load draws a given current.

stem: In the circuit shown, the input voltage rises from $10$ V to $15$ V. If the load draws a constant current of $8$ mA, find the Zener current at the new input voltage. The Zener voltage is $5$ V.

verdicts.working: At 15 V, the series-resistor current is (15−5)/250 = 40 mA. Subtract the 8 mA load current: I_Z = 32 mA.

working:
$I_s = \dfrac{15-5}{250} = 40\ \text{mA}$
$I_Z = I_s-I_L = 40-8 = 32\ \text{mA}$

Independent check: At 15 V, the series-resistor current is (15−5)/250 = 40 mA. Subtract the 8 mA load current: I_Z = 32 mA.
solution:
The series current at $V_{in}=15$ V is
$$I_s=\frac{15-5}{250}=40\text{ mA}.$$
Hence, $I_Z=I_s-I_L=40-8=32\text{ mA}$.⁨

figure.description: Draw a DC source on the left, with its positive terminal connected through a series resistor labeled R_s = 250 Ω to an output node. Connect a load branch from the output node to the source's negative return; show a downward current arrow in this branch labeled I_L = 8 mA. Connect a Zener diode in parallel with the load, with its cathode at the output node and its anode at the negative return; label it V_Z = 5 V. Label the source V_in. Show the negative return wire connecting both branches to the source's negative terminal. Do not label any branch current through the Zener.
